subject: NVDA

nodes.mechanism: CoWoS capacity is the named bottleneck in most cycles; every accelerator shipped is TSMC wafer and packaging.
nodes.observable: TSMC monthly revenue (~10 days after month end) and any CoWoS capacity comment

nodes.mechanism: HBM is the scarce input; tight supply and rising price are REVENUE to Micron and COST to NVIDIA. Same fact, opposite signs.
nodes.observable: Micron quarterly HBM commentary, contract pricing, take-or-pay terms

nodes.mechanism: Capacity named as the constraint becomes equipment orders, at a lag.
nodes.observable: WFE order commentary; TSMC/Samsung capex plans

nodes.mechanism: HBM stack build-out is disproportionately deposition and etch intensive.
nodes.observable: HBM-attributed revenue share in quarterly commentary

nodes.mechanism: Advanced packaging yield is inspection-intensive.
nodes.observable: process-control intensity commentary on advanced packaging

nodes.mechanism: Scale-out clusters need switching in near-fixed ratio to accelerators.
nodes.observable: cloud-titan revenue concentration; 800G port shipments

nodes.mechanism: Cluster size drives optical port count faster than accelerator count.
nodes.observable: datacom transceiver revenue and 800G/1.6T mix

nodes.mechanism: Same mechanism as COHR; different customer mix.
nodes.observable: cloud/datacom segment revenue

nodes.mechanism: Same edge, far smaller and noisier -- included as a HIGH-beta control: if it moves and COHR does not, the move is beta, not information.
nodes.observable: datacenter transceiver bookings

nodes.mechanism: Interconnect volume at one further remove; a slower, cleaner read.
nodes.observable: optical communications segment growth

nodes.mechanism: Rack-scale systems ship through ODMs; demand language converts to backlog.
nodes.observable: quarterly backlog and rack shipment commentary

nodes.mechanism: Same edge, larger and more diluted by a non-AI business.
nodes.observable: AI server backlog disclosure

nodes.mechanism: Smallest share of the three; the weakest version of the same edge.
nodes.observable: AI systems orders

nodes.mechanism: Power/cooling is the constraint most often named after packaging, and it is the one with the longest lead time.
nodes.observable: orders and backlog; book-to-bill

nodes.mechanism: Datacentre electrical distribution; broad industrial base dilutes it.
nodes.observable: datacentre vertical growth in segment commentary

nodes.mechanism: If POWER rather than packaging is named, this is where the constraint lands.
nodes.observable: grid equipment orders; interconnect queue commentary

nodes.mechanism: Builds the interconnect. Longest lag in the graph.
nodes.observable: backlog attributable to datacentre and transmission

nodes.mechanism: Rack density forces liquid cooling; a small, direct read.
nodes.observable: datacentre cooling revenue growth

nodes.mechanism: Two edges of OPPOSITE sign: the AI capex tide lifts it, and every custom accelerator it wins is an accelerator NVIDIA did not sell. Signed off the COMPETITION field so the two are not silently averaged.
nodes.observable: custom XPU revenue and named programme wins

nodes.mechanism: Same edge; the Google arrangement makes it the purest listed expression of substitution.
nodes.observable: custom compute revenue and programme milestones

nodes.mechanism: A buyer, not a supplier: a strong print confirms its AI revenue AND raises its cost. The sign is genuinely ambiguous and the exposure is declared LOW for exactly that reason.
nodes.observable: capex guidance, RPO/backlog, and depreciation schedule changes

nodes.mechanism: AWS backlog and 2026 capex are the largest single demand disclosure outside NVIDIA itself.
nodes.observable: AWS revenue growth, backlog, capex guide

nodes.mechanism: The one buyer that is also the substitution threat, via TPU and the Marvell arrangement.
nodes.observable: TPU deployment commentary; capex guide

nodes.mechanism: Pure buyer with no cloud resale, so its capex is the cleanest read on internally-funded demand.
nodes.observable: capex guide and depreciation life

chains: NVDA demand -> HBM -> advanced packaging -> optical -> server ODM
NVDA demand -> power -> cooling -> grid interconnect
memory inflation -> server BOM -> customer AI ROI -> capex affordability
capex affordability -> custom silicon substitution -> NVDA share
